record.title: Artificial Intelligence Strategy

english_version.by: Federal Government of Germany (Federal Ministries of Education and Research, for Economic Affairs and Energy, and of Labour and Social Affairs)

record.summary: Strategy of the German Federal Government for AI research, transfer to industry, skills and use, backed by about EUR 3 billion of federal funding to 2025. Its three equal aims are making Germany and Europe a leading AI location, responsible and public-interest-oriented development and use of AI, and embedding AI ethically, legally, culturally and institutionally in society. It commits to review the legal framework for gaps in algorithmic and AI-based decisions, to examine how AI systems can be made transparent, traceable and verifiable, and to examine state bodies and private testing institutions to oversee algorithmic decisions, with audit and impact-assessment standards.
record.notes: Prepared under the joint lead of the Federal Ministries of Education and Research, for Economic Affairs and Energy, and of Labour and Social Affairs after a nationwide online consultation, on the basis of key points the Federal Cabinet adopted on 18 July 2018. The cabinet decided the strategy on 15 November 2018; it was transmitted to the Bundesrat (Drucksache 597/18) and the Bundestag (Drucksache 19/5880). Its other governance measures include an ethics by, in and for design approach, an aim of obliging hardware and software makers to follow security by design, raising the security of AI systems against attacks, research on detecting manipulated or automatically generated content, a German AI observatory, and a roadmap on AI norms and standards with DIN, including standardised classifications of the risks associated with AI. It plans to take up the recommendations of the Data Ethics Commission and to seek common guidelines in the OECD, G7, G20 and the United Nations. The cabinet adopted an update (Fortschreibung 2020) on 2 December 2020, which raised planned federal funding to 2025 from three to five billion euros and puts new weight on pandemic response, sustainability, environmental and climate protection, and international and European networking.
record.scope_note: Mainly a national strategy for AI research, transfer to industry, skills and funding, with its safety and risk-governance content in the sections on the regulatory framework, standards and IT security; included as the Federal Government's national AI strategy.

verification.note: Stored the Bundestag printed paper 19/5880 with the full German text (48 pages), the Bundesrat printed paper 597/18 with the cover letter of the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy of 15 November 2018 stating the cabinet decision and the Bundestag number, the Federal Government's English text ('Artificial Intelligence Strategy', Status: November 2018) and German 2020 update ('Fortschreibung 2020', Stand: Dezember 2020) from ki-strategie-deutschland.de, and the Federal Government's notice of 2 December 2020 on bundesregierung.de that the cabinet adopted the update. The cover of the Bundestag paper is set in an encoded font, so its number is quoted from the Bundesrat paper. Hosts to review: dserver.bundestag.de, ki-strategie-deutschland.de and bundesregierung.de are not in pipeline/official-sites.json, so their quotes count as secondary and the computed level is C until a person records them as official for DE. The title is the Federal Government's own English title; the summary follows the German text.

judgment.status_reasoning: The cabinet decided the strategy on 15 November 2018 (Bundesrat cover letter: 'das Bundeskabinett hat in seiner heutigen Sitzung ... beschlossen', dated 15 November 2018). It calls itself the Federal Government's framework for action. The latest stored event is the cabinet's adoption of the update on Wednesday 2 December 2020 ('Das Bundeskabinett hat am Mittwoch die Fortschreibung der KI-Strategie beschlossen'), which develops the strategy further rather than replacing it. No stored source withdraws it, so Published (non-binding, current) with date_last_updated 2020-12-02.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the day of the cabinet decision, 15 November 2018, which is also the date of the ministry's transmittal letter and the date the Federal Government's notice lists. date_last_updated is the cabinet's adoption of the 2020 update on 2 December 2020; the update's own cover gives only 'Stand: Dezember 2020'.
judgment.title_reasoning: The Federal Government's English text gives the title 'Artificial Intelligence Strategy' (cover) and calls it 'The Federal Government's Artificial Intelligence (AI) strategy'; under the rule for official English titles the record uses the cover title. original_title is the German title.
judgment.identifier_reasoning: The citable reference is the Bundestag printed paper 19/5880 (the Bundesrat printed paper is 597/18, in notes).
judgment.english_version_reasoning: The English text is published by the Federal Government on the strategy's website, which the German printed paper names on every page; it is the issuer's translation of a German text, so 'government translation'.
judgment.legal_force_reasoning: A government strategy and framework for action with no legal obligations: Non-binding.
judgment.terms: Transparenz, Nachvollziehbarkeit und Überprüfbarkeit is rendered 'transparent, traceable and verifiable'; staatliche Stellen und private Prüfinstitutionen zur Kontrolle algorithmischer Entscheidungen 'state bodies and private testing institutions to oversee algorithmic decisions'; Auditierungsstandards and Standards für Folgenabschätzungen 'audit and impact-assessment standards'; Angriffssicherheit 'security against attacks'; gemeinwohlorientiert 'public-interest-oriented'.
judgment.topics_reasoning: evaluation & testing: testing institutions, audit standards and impact-assessment standards (3.9) and the examination of AI auditing in the workplace (3.5); transparency & labelling: transparency, traceability and verifiability of AI systems, information, labelling and publication duties (3.9); research priorities: research on transparency and explainability, attack security and operational safety of AI systems (3.1); public-sector use: AI in public administration and for security authorities (3.7); international cooperation: common guidelines in OECD, G7, G20 and UN and AI observatories (3.11, 3.5).
judgment.scope_reasoning: A national AI strategy whose main focus is research, industry transfer, skills and funding, with risk-governance content in its sections on adapting the regulatory framework (3.9), standards (3.10) and IT security. Under AGENTS.md section 10 and the general rules, a strategy with some safety content and a different main focus is in with a scope_note. Unlike the EU AI Continent Action Plan precedent, it sets specific governance measures (legal review, testing institutions, audit and impact-assessment standards).
